authorized by ADOH in writing, expenditures not requested within the sixty (60) day period 
after expiration of this Agreement shall be disallowed and all funds shall be reclaimed by 
ADOH. 
 
Section 14.   FUNDS RECOUPED BY RECIPIENT, INTEREST AND PROGRAM 
INCOME 
 
14.1 Definitions.  For purposes of this section, the following definitions shall apply:  
 
“Funds Recouped by Recipient” means funds initially provided by ADOH to 
Recipient under this Agreement and any matching contributions that are recouped by 
Recipient when: (1) the funds provided by ADOH under this Agreement or matching 
contributions or the proceeds of funds provided by ADOH (including, but not limited to, 
equipment or housing) do not continue to be used for an approved purpose or eligible

<!-- page 682 -->
Funding Agreement with 
State of Arizona, Department of Housing  
REV. 6/14/2023 14 
activity, as described in applicable law or regulations, for the full period of affordability 
required by this Agreement ; or (2) when a State -assisted homeownership housing does not 
continue to be the principal residence of the assisted homebuyer for the full  affordability 
period required by this Agreement.   Funds Recouped by Recipient  are subject to all the 
requirements of Program Income described below with the exception that Recipient shall not 
use Funds Recouped by Recipient  for administrative purposes.  For this reason, Recipient  
must separately account for all Funds Recouped by Recipient. 
 
“Interest” means any compensation paid or to be paid for the use or deposit of the 
funds provided by ADOH to Recipient under this Agreement. 
 
“Program Income” means gross income received by Recipient directly generated from 
the use of funds provided by ADOH under this Agreement.  When Program Income is 
generated by housing that is only partially assisted with funds provided by ADOH under this 
Agreement or matching contributions, the income shall be prorated to reflect the percentage 
of funds provided by ADOH under this Agreement.  Program Income includes, but is not 
limited to, the following: (1) proceeds from the disposition by sale or long -term lease of real 
property purchased or improved with funds provided by ADOH under this Agreement; (2) 
gross income from the use or rental of real or personal property acquired by Recipient with 
funds provided by ADOH under this Agreement, less costs incidental to generation of the 
income; (3) payments of principal and interest on loans made using funds provided by ADOH 
under this Agreement or matching contributions; (4) proceeds from the sale of loans made 
with funds provided by ADOH under this Agreement or matching contributions; (5) proceeds 
from sale of obligations secured by loans made with funds provided by ADOH under this 
Agreement or matching contributions; (6) Interest earned on Program Income pending its 
disposition; (7) proceeds from the disposition of equipment purchased with CDBG funds; (8) 
gross income from the use or rental of real property, owned by Recipient, that was constructed 
or improved with funds provided by ADOH under this Agreement, less costs incidental to 
generation of the income; (9) if the funds provided by ADOH under this Agreement are from 
the CDBG Program, funds collected through special assessments made against properties 
owned and occupied by households not of low and moderate income, where the assessments 
are used to recover all or part of the CDBG porti on of a public improvement; and (10) if the 
funds provided by ADOH under this Agreement are from the HOME Program, any other 
interest or return on the investment permitted under 24 C.F.R. Part 92.205(b) of HOME funds 
or matching contributions. 
 
14.2 Use of Program Income and Funds Recouped by Recipient.

Section 15.    DE-OBLIGATION, RECAPTURE AND REPAYMENT OF FUNDS 
 
15.1 De-obligation.  ADOH may reduce funds from the funding award evidenced

circumstances: (1) Recipient has completed performance under the Scope of Work (Attachment 
A) without using all of the fun ds provided  by ADOH under this Agreement; (2) this

a loan and Recipient or Sub-recipient paid the loan; (4) Recipient, with the consent of ADOH, 
cancelled or changed an activity required under the Scope of Work for reasons other than non-
performance; or (5) Recipient receives Program Income that has not been included in the 
budget or set forth in the Scope of Work; and (6) this Agreement has otherwise been terminated. 
ADOH may de-obligate funds under this Agreement under the foregoing circumstances upon 
written notice to Recipient.   
 
15.2 Reallocation of De -obligated HOME or State HTF Funds.   If the funds 
provided by ADOH under this Agreement are from the State HTF or  the HOME Program, 
ADOH may reallocate funds that it has de -obligated under this Agreement as it determines 
in its sole discretion.

under this Agreement are from the CDBG Progra m, ADOH may reallocate funds that it has 
de-obligated under this Agreement to Recipient from which the funds were de-obligated for 
use under an existing or new funding contract of the same funding year if Recipient  can 
immediately commit the reallocated funds to a project and execute a new or amended funding 
contract within sixty (60) calendar days of the reallocation.  If ADOH is not able to reallocate 
funds that it has de -obligated under this Agreement in accord ance with the foregoing 
sentence of this subsection, ADOH may reallocate those funds as it determines in its sole 
discretion. 
 
15.4 Recapture.  ADOH may reduce funds from the amount of the funding award 
evidenced by this Agreement, without regard to the sour ce of funding, under the following 
circumstances: (1) ADOH determines that Recipient has failed to use the funds provided by 
ADOH under this Agreement in compliance with the terms of this Agreement or the 
requirements of applicable laws and regulations (no n-compliance); or (2) Recipient fails to 
perform in accordance with the performance obligations set forth in the Scope of Work 
(Attachment A ) and the Schedule of Completion (Attachment  B) or the terms of this Agreement.  
ADOH may recapture funds under this Agreement under the foregoing circumstances upon 
written notice to Recipient.

of the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA). Pub. L. 117-58. The Act establishes a 
domestic content procurement preference, the Buy American Preference (BAP), for Federal 
programs that permit Federal financial assistance to be used for infrastructure projects. In 
Section 70912, the Act further defines a project to include “the construction, alteration, 
maintenance, or repair of infrastructure in the United States” and includes within the 
definition of infrastructure those items traditionally included along with buildings and real 
property. Starting May 14, 2022, new awards of Federal financial assistance (FFA) from a 
program for infrastructure, and any of those funds obligated by the grantee, are covered 
under the Build America, Buy America (BABA) provisions of the Act, 41 U.S.C. 8301 note. 
The waiver, published March 15, 2023, establishes a phased implementation schedule for 
application of the BAP to covered materials and HUD programs. 
 
The BAP is applicable now to iron and steel used in covered CDBG projects, i.e. for projects 
using funds obligated on or after November 15, 2022. For CPD, the BAP will apply next to 
iron and steel used in covered Recovery Housing Program (RHP) projects for funding 
obligated on or after August 23, 2023. 
… 
Additional details on fulfilling the BABA requirements can be found at 
https://www.hud.gov/program_offices/general_counsel/BABA.”

FUNDING AGREEMENT 
 
 
This AGREEMENT entered into as of this_______day of____________________, 2024 by and between 
Navajo County, 100 Code Talkers Way (P.O. Box 668), Holbrook, AZ 86025  (hereinafter referred to as 
"County”) an d Pinetop-Lakeside Senior Citizens, Inc., PO Box 1780, Lakeside, AZ  85929, which is an 
independent non-profit corporation operating under the trade name “The White Mountain Community Center” 
and will be hereinafter referred to as “WMCC”. 
 
I. COMMITMENT OF GRANT FUNDS 
The County hereby commits $131,000 in CDBG funds per Arizona Department of Housing contract for the 
replacement of the roof of WMCC located at 1594 Johnson Drive in the Town of Pinetop-Lakeside, Arizona. 
Improvements will consist of removal of WMCC’s failing asphalt shingle roofing system and installation a new 
asphalt shingle roofing system at the facility. This activity will meet the Low to Moderate Income National 
Objective (LMC) and will benefit approximately 360 people in the service area of Pinetop-Lakeside and 
nearby areas of Navajo County, of whom 308 (or 85.5%) are low-to-moderate income. 
 
II. TERM OF AGREEMENT 
The term of thi s Agreement shall commence on the date the last party executes the Agreement and shall 
commence for a term of five years after grant close- out.  The CDBG funds shall be considered a grant for as 
long as WMCC continues operation of services  according to terms of this Agreement.  The facilities must be 
used solely for the stated purpose for the term of this Agreement. 
 
III. USE OF PROPERTY 
The roof shall be used to allow WMCC to provide services  in said facility and purposes incidental thereto.  
WMCC shall not use or suffer or permit any person or group of persons to use the facility for any unlawful 
purpose or in any manner or use in violation of any covenants or restrictions of any law or ordinance of any 
governmental, political, or military order of regulations. WMCC shall abide by all civil rights laws and executive 
orders as required by the Housing and Community Development Act, as amended, and OMB Circulars, and 
other requirements as set forth by the Arizona Department of Housing CDBG Program.  
 
No uses may be for sectarian or partisan politics purposes. 
 
IV. REVERSION OF PROPERTY 
The facility is to be used for the stated purpose for a minimum of five years after grant close- out.  If the 
purpose/use will be changed, WMCC will pay the County the fair market value of the modifications. 
 
V. FEES 
All fees charged by WMCC shall be affordable to low and moderate income persons.  The County reserves 
the right to review such fees and to require adjustments if the fees are determined unaffordable to low-to-
moderate income persons. 
 
VI. RESPONSIBILITIES OF BOTH PARTIES 
A. The County shall be responsible for: 
 
1. Request and receipt of CDBG funds from the Arizona Department of Housing. 
2. Consultations with WMCC regarding project elements. 
3. Ensuring compliant procurement of the roof improvements. 
4. Ensuring compliant installation of the roof improvements.

<!-- page 708 -->
Page 2 of 4 
 
5. Record keeping, reporting, performance monitoring, and all other actions necessary 
to ensure compliance with CDBG Program requirements. 
 
B. WMCC shall be responsible for: 
 
1. Defining the specifications for the roof improvements. 
2. Assisting with some elements of the procurement and construction process, including 
conducting onsite Davis-Bacon Labor Standards interviews of workers on the project. 
3. All maintenance and future upgrades. 
4. Maintaining liability insurance. 
5. Providing any and all reports required by CDBG or the County. 
 
Any changes that involve program requirements, the purpose or location of the project, the type of project 
activity, the manner in which an activity is to be executed, a change in the final outcom e, a change of entity 
ownership or of beneficiary of the activity, as well as any revisions to the Responsibilities of Both Parties 
require written amendment to this Agreement. 
 
VII. OWNERSHIP OF PROPERTY 
WMCC shall own the roof improvements.  
  
VIII. INSURANCE 
 
WMCC shall provide, by self -insurance or other means, and maintain and/or cause its subcontractors to 
provide and maintain appropriate insurance.  In no event shall the total coverage be less than the minimum 
insurance coverage specified below: 
(1) Commercial General Liability in an amount not less than $1,000,000.   WMCC shall name the 
County, its agents, officials and employees as additional insureds and shall specify t hat the insurance 
afforded by WMCC shall be primary insurance and that any insurance coverag e carried or self -insurance by 
the County, any department or any employee shall be excess coverage and not contributory insurance to that 
provided by WMCC.  Said policy shall contain a severability of interest provision.  The County reserves the 
right to c ontinue payment of premium for which reimbursement shall be deducted from amounts due or 
subsequently due WMCC. 
 
Failure on the part of WMCC to procure and maintain the required liability insurance and provide proof thereof 
to the County within ten days following the commencement of a new policy, shall constitute a material breach  
of t he Agreement upon which the County  may immediately terminate the Agreement.  Within ten day s of 
signing the Agreement, WMCC shall furnish the County with copies of the Certificate of Insurance drawn in 
conformity with the above i nsurance requirements.  The County  reserves the right to request and receive 
certified copies of any or all of the above policies and/or endorsements. 
 
WMCC agrees to comply w ith statutory requirements for Workers'  Compensation and unemployment 
insurance coverage during term of this Agreement.  A Certificate of Insurance for Workers' Compensation 
coverage naming the County as additional insured shall be provided within ten days  of signing this 
Agreement. 
 
IX. TERMINATION OF CONTRACT 
Any party to this Agreement may terminate said Agreement without cause by giving the other parties thirty 
days written notice of intent to terminate.  In the event WMCC elects to terminate without cause, WMCC may 
be liable to repay to the County funds equal to the current market value of the work. 
 
If any party violates the terms or conditions of this Agreement, the other parties may give thirty days written 
notice of such violation or default.  If WMCC is the defaulting party and fails to commence to cure the default 
within thirty days of written notice, the County may declare the Agreement terminated.  At such time WMCC 
shall have no rights under this Agreement and may be liable to repay the County funds equal to the current 
market value of the work.

<!-- page 709 -->
Page 3 of 4 
 
The Agreement may be terminated per ARS 38-511, Conflict of Interest. 
 
X. ASSIGNMENT AND SUBLETTING 
WMCC shall not be permitted to assign, sublet, or otherwise transfer in any manner any of its rights under this 
Agreement without the express written consent of the County. 
 
XI. INDEMNIFICATION 
WMCC agrees to save and hold harmless the County and/or any of its agents, officials and employees from 
any and all claims, demands, suits, actions, proceedings, law s, costs, and/or damages of every kind and 
description including any attorney's fees and/or litigation expenses which may be brought or made against or 
incurred by the County on account of  loss of or damage to any property or for injuries to or death of a ny 
person caused by, arising out of, or contributed to, in whole or in part, by reason of any alleged act, omission, 
or professional error, fault , mistake, or negligence of WMCC, its employees, agents, or representatives, or 
subcontractors, their employees, agents, or representatives in connection with or incident to the performance 
of this Agreement or arising out of Workers' Compensation claims, Unemployment Compensation claims, or 
Unemployment Disability Compensation claims of employees of WMCC and/or its subcontractors or claims 
under similar  such laws or obligations.  WMCC's obligations under this paragraph shall not extend to any 
liability caused by the sole negligence of the County or its employees. 
 
XII. ATTORNEY'S FEES 
In any action between the parties to this Agreement, their heirs, executors, administrators, or permitted 
assigns, for a default, breach, or for the enforcement of any of the terms and conditions of this Agreement, 
any reasonable attorneys' fees to be fixed by the courts having juris diction of the action shall be added to and 
made a part of the allowable cost in such action in favor of the successful party.  
 
XIII. ARBITRATION 
In the event of any controversy which may arise out of this Agreement the parties agree to abide by arbitration 
as set forth in the Arizona Revised Statutes.

Board of Supervisors Regular 3. a. 1.        
Meeting Date: 02/27/2024  
Title: Amendment No. 2 Navajo County Jail Medical and Psychological Services
Submitted By: Cheryl Hollins, Account Specialist
Department: Navajo County Jail District
Motion before the Board:
Amendment No. 2 extending Navajo County Jail Medical and Psychological Services Contract with
Wexford Health Sources, Inc. for one additional year (March 8, 2024 through March 7, 2025)
Background:
On March 8, 2022 the Board of Directors approved the contract with Wexford Health Source, Inc. This
contract has worked well for the Navajo County Jail District. This contract may be renewed up to four
additional one-year terms. This would be the second renewal and both parties are in concurrence. Staff
recommends that the contract be extended for one additional year.

Board of Supervisors Regular 4. a. 1.        
Meeting Date: 02/27/2024  
Title: Community Library Update
Submitted For: Jennifer Volkert, Library District Director 
Submitted By: Melissa Buckley, Clerk of the Board of Supervisors
Department: NC Library District
Presented By: Jennifer Volkert
Subject:
Presentation and recognition of the following Community Libraries: Pinedale Public Library, Clay
Springs Public Library, Rim Community Library, and Woodruff Community Library. 
Background: 
Navajo County Library District has four member libraries that are solely operated on a volunteer basis.
These libraries do not have a book and materials, payroll, or supply and services budget. Navajo County
has given these libraries annual support for more than a decade. We appreciate our volunteer's
commitment to running their community library as efficiently and effectively as our larger municipal
libraries.

Board of Supervisors Regular 6. a.        
Meeting Date: 02/27/2024  
Title: Navajo County Complex Remodel Contract No. B23-09-021
Submitted For: Grant Evans, Capital Projects Manager 
Submitted By: Cheryl Hollins, Account Specialist
Department: Administrative Services
Presented By: Grant Evans
Motion before the Board:
Consideration of award of Contract No. B23-09-021 for the Navajo County Complex Remodel to Pointe
Companies, Inc and to authorize change order authority to the County Manager for 10% of the contract
amount, and authorize the County Manager to execute the necessary documents.
Background:
This contract will provide for construction services for the remodel of the Navajo County Complex.  This
remodel will simplify and improve customer access to services, improve safety and security, create a
more functional training space and remodel the restrooms to update them and improve their functionality.
Sealed proposals were received by the Board of Supervisors at the Navajo County Government Center,
Holbrook, Arizona until 3:00 p.m. M.S.T., February 1, 2024.  No bids were accepted after 3:00 p.m.
M.S.T..  The bid was publicly opened and read aloud at 3:15 p.m.  One bid was received and Pointe
Companies, Inc. is the responsible, responsive bidder.  
Recommendation: 
Staff is recommending award of Contract B23-09-021 Navajo County Complex Remodel to Pointe
Companies, Inc.
Fiscal Impact
Fiscal Year: 2024
Budgeted Y/N: Y
Amount Requested: 511,500
Fiscal Impact:
The total amount requested is $511,500.  $465,000 for the construction contract and $46,500 (10%) as a
reserve fund for project changes.
There are three funding sources for this project, which include $150,000 from ARPA Funds, $150,000
from General Funds and $211,500 from Local Assistance Consistency Funds (LACF).

CONTRACT 
 
THIS CONTRACT is made and entered into as of February 27, 2024 (the “Effective Date”) 
by and between Navajo County (“County”) and Pointe Companies, Inc (“Contractor”). 
 
1. SCOPE OF WORK:  Contractor shall furnish any and all materials, equipment and labor 
required for performing all work for NAVAJO COUNTY COMPLEX REMODEL, 
CONTRACT, #B23-09-021, in accordance with the Contract Documents, in a workmanlike 
manner to the satisfaction of County through its County Engineer. 
 
2. CONTRACT DOCUMENTS:  The Contract Documents comprise this Contract and the 
attached  Notice of Invitation for Bids,  General Provisions, , Proposal dated 
January 31, 2024,  Bid Schedule (Item No. 1 Only),  Bid Bond,  Affidavit of Non-
Collusion,  Subcontractor Certification,  Qualifications/Projects/References,  
Performance Bond,  Labor and Materials Bond ,  Contractor Performance Warranty, 
 Certificate of Insurance,  Plans, and addenda thereto, if any.  If there is any conflict in 
the documents, this Contract shall control over all others; the Specifications shall control 
over the General Provisions and Special Provisions; and the Special Provisions shall 
control over the General Provisions. 
 
3. NO LIENS / TIME FOR COMPLETION:  Contractor shall furnish all materials, equipment 
and labor in accordance with the Contract Documents free and clear of all claims, liens 
and charges whatsoever, within the time, or times, stated in the Proposal. 
 
4. CANCELLATION:  This Contract is subject to cancellation pursuant to A.R.S. § 38-511 
(concerning conflicts of interest). 
 
5. PAYMENTS:   County shall pay to Contractor a not-to-exceed sum of four hundred sixty-
five thousand dollars ($465,000.00) as payment in full for all services rendered by 
Contractor pursuant to this Agreement.  Payment shall be made on the basis of the 
progress and completion of tasks in accordance with the Work to substantiate the 
percentage of completion of Work during the time period covered by the Invoice.  No later 
than 14 days after each invoice has been verified and approved by the Engineer, County 
shall pay to Contractor ninety (90%) of the value of said work in place, as approved by the 
Engineer.  The balance of ten percent (10%) shall be retained by the Owner until the time 
of final payment and acceptance of said work, as per A.R.S. §34-221.  The provisions of 
A.R.S. §34-221 are incorporated herein by this reference and shall control in regard to all 
matters of payment. 
 
6. CERTIFICATIONS:  
 
A. A. PROHIBITION OF BOYCOTT OF ISRAEL:  Contractor certifies that neither it nor 
its subcontractors are currently or will be engaged in, for the duration of this Contract 
engage in, a boycott of Israel as defined by A.R.S. § 35-393 et seq.  Violation of this 
certification may result in an action by the County up to and including termination of 
the Contract. 
 
B. WRITTEN CERTIFICATION PURSUANT TO A.R.S. §35-394:  Pursuant to A.R.S. § 
35-394, Contractor certifies that it is not currently using, and agrees for the duration 
of this Agreement to not use (1) the forced labor of ethnic Uyghurs in the People’s 
Republic of China; (2) any goods or services produced by the forced labor of ethnic

Board of Supervisors Regular 7. a.        
Meeting Date: 02/27/2024  
Title: March 19, 2024 Poll Workers and Vote Center Locations
Submitted By: Rayleen Richards, Elections Director
Department: Elections
Presented By: Rayleen Richards
Motion before the Board:
Consideration and adoption of Resolution Number 09-2024, designating polling places/vote centers for
the March 19, 2024, Presidential Preference Election and a polling location contingency plan and poll
workers. 
Background:
Pursuant to A.R.S. § 16-531
  
When an election is ordered, and not less than twenty days prior to a general or primary election,
the board of supervisors shall appoint for each election precinct one inspector, one marshal, two
judges and as many clerks of election as deemed necessary.
1.
Pursuant to A.R.S. § 16-411
  
Not less than twenty days before a general or primary election, and at least ten days before a
special election, the board shall designate one polling place within each precinct where the election
shall be held, except that:
2.
On a specific finding of the board, included in the order or resolution designating polling places pursuant
to this subsection, that no suitable polling place is available within a precinct, a polling place for such
precinct may be designated within an adjacent precinct.
Recommendation: 
Staff Recommends

RESOLUTION NO ______ - 24 
A RESOLUTION OF THE NAVAJO COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS, 
DESIGNATING POLLING PLACES/VOTE CENTERS, PURSUANT TO ARS § 16-411(B). 
WHEREAS, ARS § 16-411(B) provides as follows with respect to designating polling places: 
     “Not less than twenty days before a general or primary election, and at least ten days before a special election, the 
board shall designate one polling place within each precinct where the election shall be held, except that: 1.On a specific 
finding of the board, included in the order or resolution designating polling places pursuant to this subsection, that no 
suitable polling place is available within a precinct, a polling place for such precinct may be designated within an adjacent 
precinct. 
  and 
WHEREAS, on a specific resolution of the board, the board may authorize the use of voting centers in place of or in addition 
to specifically designated polling place. A voting center shall allow any voter in the county to receive the appropriate ballot 
for that voter on Election Day and lawfully cast the ballot. The voting center may be established in coordination and 
consultation with the county recorder, at other county offices or at other location in the county deemed appropriate. 
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED by the Board of Supervisors as follows: 
That polling locations/vote centers for all Navajo County voting precincts attached hereto and incorporated herein as 
“Exhibit A” and contingency plan herein as “Exhibit B”, are hereby approved by the Navajo County Board of Supervisors.

Board of Supervisors Regular 7. b.        
Meeting Date: 02/27/2024  
Title: SCFCD - Appointment of BOD 
Submitted By: Melissa Buckley, Clerk of the Board of Supervisors
Department: Elections
Presented By: Rayleen Richards
Motion before the Board:
Consideration and appointment of two members to fill the vacant seats on the Silver Creek Flood Control
District Board of Directors. 
Background:
The Silver Creek Flood Control District did not hold an election in October 2023, leaving two vacant
seats; therefore, the Board of Supervisors needs to appoint qualified candidates to the position. The Silver
Creek Flood Control District as well as Navajo County has requested that interested members submit a
letter of interest to the Navajo County Board of Supervisors. We have received three letters of interest.
48-2681. Election of directors; qualification; vacancies
A. In each district organized under this chapter an election shall be held on the first Wednesday in
October of the calendar year next succeeding that in which the organization of the district is completed,
and on the first Wednesday in October each second year thereafter, at which one or more directors for the
district as provided in section 48-2607 shall be elected to fill the vacancy or vacancies occurring on the
board by expiration of the term of office of one or more members of the board as provided in section
48-2615. The persons receiving the highest number of votes for the offices to be filled at the election
shall be declared elected thereto.
B. Within ten days after receiving their respective certificates of election, each of the persons elected shall
qualify as a director by taking and subscribing the official oath and filing a bond as provided by this
section. Each director shall execute an official bond in the amount of one thousand dollars, which shall be
approved by the judge of the superior court in the county where the organization of the district was
affected, and recorded in the office of the county recorder of such county. The official bond together with
the official oath shall be filed with the secretary of the board of directors. Official bonds shall be in the
form prescribed by law for official bonds of county officers.
C. If a vacancy occurs on the board of directors, it shall be filled by appointment by the board of
supervisors of the county in which the district is organized. A director so appointed shall qualify
within ten days after receiving notice of his appointment in the same manner as provided for
directors elected to the office, and shall hold office only until the next regular election for the
district and until his successor is elected and qualified.
 
Recommendation: 
Staff recommends appointment of two members. 
Gus Lundberg is currently serving on the SCFCD Board and seeking reappointment.

Board of Supervisors Regular 8. a.        
Meeting Date: 02/27/2024  
Title: Approval to enter into Agreement with APS Solar Communities
Submitted For: Bret Starns, Facilities Management Director 
Submitted By: Michelle Marquardt, Office Manager
Department: Facilities Mangement
Presented By: Bret Starns
Motion before the Board:
Consideration of an agreement with the APS Solar Communities Program to install covered solar parking
structures in the Employee Parking lot at the Navajo County Governmental Complex in Holbrook. 
Background:
The APS Solar Communities program is open to customers that serve the limited-income population,
including Title I schools, nonprofits and rural governments.
The program will include the installation of a solar system that will include mounting of the parking
shade structure, installation of additional conduit for power, communications and sensors, solar PV
modules and LED lighting on the structure. In exchange for the generated power, APS will give a bill
credit. The bill credit will be valued by the size of your parking structure solar system ($2.5/kW). For
example, a 50 kW system would be a $125/monthly bill credit.
Eligibility
• Have enough outdoor space to accommodate a minimum 50kW or larger size system (about 20 parking
spots).
Recommendation: 
We recommend that the Board approves this agreement so that we can move forward with this project.

APS Solar Communities Program Agreement 
Rural Government Municipality 
 
 This Agreement is entered into as of     , 2024 by and between 
Arizona Public Service Company, an Arizona corporation (“APS”), and NAVAJO 
COUNTY (“Customer”), a rural government. APS and Customer may be referred to herein 
individually as a “Party” and collectively as the “Parties.” 
 
RECITALS  
 
A. By Decision No. 76295 (August 2017), the ACC (Arizona Corporation 
Commission) approved a program now known as the APS Solar Communities 
Program (the “Program”). APS is implementing the Program for utility-owned 
solar distributed generation on covered parking at the Property listed in Section 1. 
The purpose of this program is to expand access to solar for limited and moderate-
income Arizonans. 
 
B. “System” is defined as a solar photovoltaic generation Facility.  
 
C.  For a period of 20 years following installation by APS of the System, APS will 
own and operate the System at the Property.  At the end of the term APS, unless 
the parties agree otherwise, as set forth below, APS will remove the Systems and 
return the site back to its original condition, with normal wear and tear excepted.  
 
D. At the end of the term, the Parties may agree in writing to: (1) extend the Program 
or (2) transfer ownership of the System to Customer. 
 
E. Customer desires to have a System installed on its property and will comply with 
the terms and conditions set forth below. 
 
F. “Rural Government” means rural Arizona incorporated cities and towns with 
populations of less than 150,000 not contiguous with or situated within a Metro 
Area.  
 
The parties agree as follows: 
 
1. APS will install an approximately 290 ACkW System on property owned by 
Customer and located at 100 Code Talker Ln, Holbrook, AZ 86025 (the 
“Property”).  The terms and conditions of the installation will be contained in a 
separate agreement between APS and a licensed installer that meets utility 
qualification criteria through RFP (Request for Proposal) process. APS will 
own, operate, and maintain the System.    
 
2. APS will pay all costs associated with the installation, ownership, operation, 
and maintenance of the System.

<!-- page 775 -->
3. APS will install the lighting fixtures attached to the parking structure and will 
be responsible for the operation and maintenance of the lighting fixtures for the 
first 3 years. Customer acknowledges, however, that APS’s inspection of the 
lighting fixtures will only occur once annually and that Customer is responsible, 
during its routine maintenance of its property, for notifying APS if it observes 
that the lighting is off or not working. Following the 3-year period, Customer 
shall be solely responsible for the installation, operation, and maintenance of 
the lighting fixtures. 
 
4. Customer desires to participate in the APS Solar Communities program and 
agrees to allow APS to install, own, operate and maintain the System at the 
Property for the purpose of generating electricity that will be delivered to the 
APS grid.  Customer agrees to reasonably cooperate with APS, APS’s installer, 
and any subcontractor in order to facilitate timely installation of the System.   
 
5. Customer will grant APS an easement in the form attached to this agreement as 
Exhibit A, on the Property for the purpose of installing, owning, operating, and 
maintaining a System.   
 
6. 20 Year Term; Property Ownership Transfers. The agreement will run for a 
term of 20 years from the date the solar array is installed. At the end of this 
agreement, APS will remove the solar array at its cost. If the ownership of the 
property changes, through a sale or otherwise, the subsequent property owner 
may elect to execute this same agreement in their name. If the subsequent 
property owner decline participation in the program, APS will remove the solar 
array at its cost.  
 
7. In exchange for the installation of the System, for so long as this agreement is 
in effect, Customer will receive a monthly incentive, at the rate of $2.50 per kW 
as referenced in Section 1 (example: 100kW @ $2.50 = $250 monthly 
incentive) for participation in this Program.  
 
8. The Parties agree that APS may need to disclose the information in connection 
with its regulatory filing or to otherwise satisfy its regulatory requirements. In 
the event that APS intends to disclose any of the Information to the ACC, or 
any employee, staff member, consultant, or agent thereof, it shall give Customer 
prompt prior written notice of its intention so that Customer may seek a 
protective order or other appropriate remedy. In the event that a protective order 
or other remedy is not obtained, Customer waives APS’ compliance with the 
terms hereof with respect to such information. Nothing herein shall be deemed 
to permit Customer to disclose the Information to the ACC, or any other party, 
unless such disclosure is otherwise permitted herein. The Parties understand 
and agree that Customer is subject to Arizona’s Public Records Law and 
Customer may not keep information related to this Agreement confidential 
unless explicitly authorized by Arizona’s Public Records Law. 
 
9. This Agreement shall become effective upon execution by both Parties. 
 
10. This Agreement is a binding contract. To the extent that either Party incurs any 
costs in connection with this Agreement or the subject matter hereof, such costs 
shall not be reimbursable by the other Party.

<!-- page 776 -->
11. This Agreement is subject to cancellation for conflict of interest pursuant to 
A.R.S. § 38-511. 
 
12. Either APS or the Customer may terminate this agreement upon providing 90 
days’ advance written notice to the other party.  Upon termination by either 
party, APS will remove the solar array at its cost.  As of the effective date of 
the termination, APS will no longer pay the monthly incentive to the Customer 
and APS’ easement shall terminate.  Upon termination of the agreement, APS 
agrees to promptly execute all documentation necessary to terminate APS’ 
easement.  
 
13. All notices under this Agreement shall be provided to Parties as follows: 
a. Customer: 
i. NAVAJO COUNTY 
b. APS: 
i. apssolarcommunities@aps.com 
 
14. This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement of the Parties with respect to 
its subject matter and supersedes all other oral or written representations.

ADHS will fund the Navajo County Health Department to lead this activity to implement an integrated 
approach to address chronic disease and other underlying health issues (e.g., mental health issues, 
substance abuse) that predispose people to an adverse outcome from COVID-19 infection. 
 
Navajo County is a vast rural community that has a significant shortage of qualified behavioral health 
providers, substance abuse resources/treatment and medical specialists. Some of the barriers include 
but are not limited to: eligibility requirements, waiting lists, limited transportation, long distances to 
access services, inadequate mental health and substance abuse treatment, insurance coverage and 
other issues with access to care making it very difficult for those with challenges or needing to access 
mental health, substance abuse assistance/intervention and specialized healthcare services to obtain 
care and access resources. Covid-19 has significantly increased mental health and substance abuse 
issues due to increased stress, loss of loved ones, fear, change and social isolation. A high percentage 
of Navajo County residents who contracted the COVID-19 virus are experiencing long-term sequela and 
residual effects that impact their quality of life and increase their need to access specialized medical 
care. Currently, there is lack of funding and resources to support a preventative approach to mental well 
being, as well as to managing chronic conditions. Identifying resources and facilitating a community 
approach to navigate the referral and linkage to care process is greatly needed, as is a network of 
qualified and competent professionals to assist those needing to access services. For example, the 
mental health council consists of several agencies partnering to address mental health issues and 
concerns in our community. However, there is not one specific agency dedicated to this and ensuring 
the strategies are met and evaluated.

This program would designate trained staff, dedicated to facilitating mental health first aid trainings for 
adults and individuals that serve youth in our community to include but not limited to: school personnel, 
families, veterans, homeless individuals, and senior adults. We intend on increasing school participation 
in Creating Safe Spaces a peer to peer program for adolescents to address mental health and a 
neighbor to neighbor program for senior adults. It would also allow for expansion of our existing chronic 
disease programs to include the addition of a public health nurse to better facilitate assisting those with 
complex chronic conditions to better manage their specific health concerns to avoid exacerbations. 
Program staff would identify local, state and national mental health, substance abuse and chronic 
disease resources our community could utilize and help work on a coordinated referral process to link 
these individuals to care and services. In July 2021, Navajo County Health Department will receive 
minimal funding to start a local suicide fatality review team through Navajo County Public Health. The 
review team will make recommendations on programs and strategies in effort of reducing suicide related 
deaths and other self-harming risk behaviors. Navajo County currently receives no funding for mental 
health and limited minimal funding for injury prevention. This will allow prevention educational programs, 
media awareness campaigns, mental health first aid trainings, safe spaces training (a peer-based 
mental health approach), trauma-informed care training, stress resiliency training for our community. 
Funding would be utilized to develop a death review program. Navajo County currently has a child 
fatality review team and an overdose review team. If the need is identified and found this approach 
would be beneficial, funding would be used to implement a maternal death review team. This funding will 
also be used to sustain a suicide death review team, allowing us to develop a comprehensive approach 
to addressing mortality issues in our community, especially where they intersect, and apply to those with 
health disparities.

Navajo County is a rural county with several food deserts, high poverty rates, and limited community 
resources. One in three Navajo County residents live in poverty. Navajo County has higher 
unemployment rates and lower median income rates than the Arizona statewide average. Food scarcity 
impacts all age groups negatively; contributing to high rates of obesity, chronic disease, and other social 
determinants of health. These already existing concerns were further complicated during the COVID-19 
pandemic due to increased poverty and other social determinates of health related to job losses and 
increased medical costs. It also placed greater strain on our community and civic organizations 
(homeless organizations/shelters, food banks and other social services) who provide resources to these 
at-risk populations, due to an increased number of individuals accessing their resources during the 
pandemic. Navajo County Health Department currently has very limited existing resources that they can 
access/utilize to address these issues. This grant funding would allow for a nutrition program manager to 
connect these agencies and help take the programs to another level by educating and providing technical 
assistance to communities and tribal partners on how to grow food and establishing community gardens 
to have a healthy, sustainable food source in food deserts. Navajo County Health Department (NCHD) 
will align these efforts with Meals on Wheels, NACOG, senior centers, towns/cities, and other existing 
programs to provide nutritious meals to seniors or disabled populations living in poverty or homebound. 
This provides not only nutrition but companionship to reduce mental health issues that have also 
increased during the COVID-19 pandemic due to social isolation. NCHD will work with local collaborative 
partners to increase accessibility to healthy foods, accompanied with nutritional literacy activities to aid in 
budgeting skills to use financial resources to make healthier food purchases. Local exploration of the 
impact of substance abuse and poor nutrition and their impact on overall health and chronic conditions 
will also be assessed and intervention strategies with measurable outcomes will be established to 
address identified needs. NCHD currently serves on the White Mountain Meals on Wheels as a board 
member, participates in the Southern Feeding collaboration, and has strong relationships with senior 
centers across rural Navajo County. This funding would allow them to strengthen these partnerships; 
assist in bridging the community gaps to better meet the needs of county residents to mitigate the 
economic impact of the pandemic and empower the community to make healthier food selections 
impacting chronic disease, diabetes, and obesity rates.

Navajo County contains three of the largest tribal nations: Hopi, White Mountain Apache and the Navajo 
Nation. It is estimated 45.7% of Navajo County's population is American Indian, per the 2019 US Census. 
Our Hispanic population is 11.5%. The Navajo Nation was one of the most significantly impacted 
populations in the US, in relation to burden of COVID-19. When assessing the social vulnerability index for 
household income and household size, 7 of the top 30 zip codes in Arizona fall within Navajo County. Of 
those 7 zip codes, 6 are on tribal lands.

per square mile is 10.8 people. While unemployment soared in response to COVID pandemic, poverty was 
prevalent in Navajo County well before the COVID pandemic started, with 28% of residents living in poverty 
and 9% of those being 65 and older (Source US Census ACS 5-YR). Internal surveys of our citizens post-
covid infection reveals that 33% of those infected experienced moderate to severe infection and that after 
surveying 10% of all infected, to-date, 100% of those who experienced moderate to severe infection suffer

Navajo County is a rural county with limited data collection and data analysis resources. Navajo County has 
recruited for an epidemiologist several times in the past. Due to limited funds and a small rural community with 
few amenities, interest has been underwhelming. This has hampered their ability to address the COVID-19 
pandemic and other local epidemics. 
 
Navajo County Public Health would like build out their in-house epidemiological team to meet the county’s needs 
in a sustainable way. To do this, they plan to: 1. Provide tuition reimbursement with a retention commitment to 
their infectious disease nurse who has agreed to expand her knowledge and epidemiological skills by pursing a 
post-graduate degree, with an emphasis in epidemiology. 2. Add two office support staff to the Navajo County epi 
team to aid with data entry and continue to support their professional growth and capacity. 3. Update their 
electronic medical records (EMS) systems and data dashboards. 
 
With increased workforce capacity and data platform capacity, they will be better prepared to meet the needs of 
their rural and medically underserved community.With increased workforce capacity and data platform capacity, 
they will be better prepared to meet the needs of their rural and medically underserved community. The 
milestones are as follows: 1) Initiate and complete personnel development 2) Obtain licenses and training for 
platforms that include data reporting, client scheduling and data reporting/sharing capabilities. 3) Provide funding 
to contract a grant writer to aid them in finding and securing additional grant opportunities geared towards 
addressing health disparities and serving the needs of high risk and under-served populations, allowing us to 
sustain the activities and measures established and implemented with this funding.

Navajo County Health Department will develop and sustain a community health outreach liaison 
program. The team will be led by a public health nurse (PHN), who would also serve as the tribal 
liaison and healthcare liaison. This PHN would interface with and represent the more complex tribal 
and medical view points and pieces of the group. 
 
For the purposes of this program, Navajo County would be divided into three regions: 1. 
Holbrook/Winslow region, 2. Heber/Snowflake/Taylor region and 3. Lakeside/Pinetop/Show Low 
region. A community outreach liaison would be hired for each of these regions. Primary focus areas 
for these liaisons would be to: establish/facilitate two-way communication, engage schools/local 
governments/healthcare partners/community/organization partners, leveraging with partners to expand 
existing initiatives/strategies that are part of our CHIP, provide education, support local 
coalitions/community groups, linkage to care, empower and unite the community as a whole to 
leverage/conserve resources and maximize improved health outcomes.

involvement and participation in community CHA/CHIP 4. Assess impacts of COVID-19 to citizens and 
communities throughout Navajo County 5. Work with local media to educate the community on social 
determinants of health.

Board of Supervisors Regular 9. a. 2.        
Meeting Date: 02/27/2024  
Title: FDA Retail Program Standards Grant Funding Received
Submitted For: Janelle Linn, Health Director 
Submitted By: Kathryn Mathewson, Environmental Health Program Manager
Department: NC Public Health Services District Division: Code Enforcement Division
Motion before the Board:
Approval of funds provided to Navajo County Public Health Services District, Environmental Program,
due to the adoption of the Food, Drug and Administration Retail Program Standards in the amount up to
$31,500
Background:
In October 2022, we updated our Environmental Health ordinance No. PSHD 01-09 to include the 2017
Food Code and the FDA Retail Program Standards. The FDA Retail Program Standards allows Navajo
County to become consistent with other food safety programs throughout the United States. Navajo
County was recently provided funds up to $31,500 which can be utilized for inspection equipment,
training and development, and deliverables to complete standardization. Meeting the first phase of
deliverables made our EH Program eligible for this funding.  This is only one step of the funding
available through the FDA Retail Program Standards, and we will be applying for future funding
opportunities as we continue to move forward in the standardization process.
Fiscal Impact
Fiscal Year: 2023-2024
Budgeted Y/N: N
Amount Requested:
Fiscal Impact:
This will increase our operational spending by $31,500. Below is a summary of the grant that was awarded
and will be fixed funded based on deliverables met (we would be able to complete Standard 1, 3 &4) in the
standardization process. 
• Support for work on Standards 1-8 (Required Outcome) - $5,000 Fixed Funding
• Support for work on Standard 9 in pursuit of a Public Health Metric (Optional
Outcome, but highly encouraged) - $5,000 Fixed Funding
• Participate as a Mentee in the NACCHO-led Mentorship Program - $14,000 Fixed
Funding
• Support for Retail Food Safety Trainings, Conferences, and Workshops – Up to
$7,500 Traditional Reimbursement

Voluntary National Retail Food Regulatory Program Standards 
Grant Type: 2024 Track 2 Development Base 
Amount Requested: $31,500.00 
Amount Awarded: $31,500.00 
Project Summary: We plan to meet/audit S1, S3, and S8 by developing new policies and acquiring inspection equipment 
needed to carry out regulatory duties. In addition, we will partially meet S2, S4, S5, and S6 by sending staff members to a 
Retail Food Safety conference, conducting file reviews/statistical analyses, and collaborating with a mentor. We will also 
work on S9 by implementing a baseline risk factor study. Once complete, we will develop criteria to help establishments 
and staff to prevent FBI.

2023 Healthy Forest Initiative Grant Agreement 23-201 in the amount of $115,000
Background:
Navajo County Emergency Management has been awarded $115,000 under the Healthy Forest Initiative
Grant. This grant funds the mitigation of the threat of wildfire on private property throughout Navajo
County's Wildland Urban Interface. Each year, Navajo County Emergency Management continues to find
ways to protect the citizens of our county from the threats that would have the most impact, including
wildfire, flood and severe winter weather. This continued effort to protect the lives, homes and businesses
in our community is one important step forward in our mitigation efforts.

improved fire control technologies, organization of shared fire suppression resources, 
forestry resources planning, conservation of forest land, and achievement of a number of 
other goals for the use and protection of forest lands. This agreement is a sub-award of

4. Project Lead (250 Character Max)
Catrina Jenkins, Emergency Manager, has been lead for these grant applications for the past 6 years. Navajo County has
successfully been awarded in 2017, 2018, 2021 and 2022 and have/will provided mitigation of wildfire for nearly 900 acres.
5. Acres to be Treated

Hand and Mechanical, Hand Thinning, Mechanical
7. Center Coordinates and PDF Map (0-10 points, 25 character max)
34.344841, -110.291391
8. Project Overview and Area Description (0-10 points, 600 character max)
Navajo County seeks to continue the mitigation of wildfire through thinning of private property throughout the Wildland Urban 
Interface adjacent to both USFS Apache-Sitgreaves Forests and several state land forests. The southern area of Navajo County is 
thickly forested and is the primary focus of  this application as highlighted in the 2016 Sitgreaves CWPP (map attached). 
According to AzWRAP the residential areas highlighted are all within areas considered to be in varying degrees wildfire threat. 
Navajo County continues to partner with USFS and AzDFFM to promote and partner in mitigation. 
9. Project Objectives and Deliverables (0-15 points, 850 character max)
Navajo County has identified 70 acres on private property throughout several communities and subdivisions. This project will 
continue to build on progress made in previous projects in conjunction with partnering agencies projects. Navajo County will look 
to have between 5-25 acres completed each quarter as weather allows and will work to complete all 70 acres by the end of the 
program period of performance. 
10. Scope of Work and Project Timeline (0-20 points, 1,100 character max)
Navajo County continues to conduct outreach and education throughout the region in order to continually add participants for 
future projects. Participants are in the form of private property owners and Home Owners Associations. Participants receive an 
initial assessment and prescriptions from staff and once the project is final, staff completes the marking of trees and provides the 
current list of contractors throughout the area that are able to provide the work prescribed. Property owners are responsible for 
the full 30% match and any additional costs above the $2,275 per acre cap. Once the contractor completes the work and the 
invoice is paid, property owners will provide all required documentation to staff to submit for eligible reimbursement. Navajo 
County will continue to provide timely reports and reimbursement requests on a quarterly basis.                 
11. Collaboraton, Partners and Beneficiaries (0-15 points, 600 character max)
All projects are within the identified WUI areas included in the Navajo County Sitgreaves CWPP. All of these areas are identified as 
adjoining State, USFS or BLM lands. Navajo County will continue to foster our partnerships with all of these agencies as well as the
HOA's, local contractors, fire response agencies and more as all of these partners are required to aid in the mitigation of wildfire.

<!-- page 807 -->
12. Sustainability (0-15 points, 600 character max)
Navajo County staff continues to promote defensible space, Fire Adapted Communities and Firewise programs throughout the 
county. Many of the partners throughout Navajo County continue to support these efforts with additional education on our behalf. 
In addition, before property owners are provided funding, they are required to acknowledge that federal funding will not be 
available to re-treat the same acres for 2 years. This promotes property owner accountability and continues sustainability. Finally, 
many of our participants further educate neighbors and family/friends on these benefits.

<!-- page 814 -->
Navajo County 2023 HFI Narrative  
 
Navajo County - For Official Use Only 
Scope of Work 
Navajo County is looking to mitigate the threat of wildfire  approximately 70 acres 
throughout the southern communities of Navajo County including Pinetop-Lakeside, Show 
Low, Pinedale-Claysprings, and several subdivisions throughout the area where the primary 
vegetation type consists of Ponderosa pine with a thick understory of Alligator, Utah, One-
Seed, and Rocky Mountain junipers, Gamble and Live/Shrub oak, and Manzanita. All of the 
properties in the proposed project are individually/privately owned and Homeowner 
Associations. There are properties as small as a tenth of an acre up to 10 acres in size. Each 
property will be assessed, and a prescription written based on an 80-basal formula 
wherever possible. All properties are adjacent to or within the designated WUI boundaries 
as described in the Navajo County CWPP’s and/or the Navajo County Multi-Jurisdiction 
Hazard Mitigation Plan. 
 
Navajo County will provide a list of approved contractors to the property owners to use to 
obtain 3 quotes to select from. Additionally, Navajo County will maintain cooperation. It is 
estimated that costs for treating these properties will be $2,275 per acre. While some 
properties may not require the entire amount per acre there will be some with higher costs. 
  
Navajo County will provide the assessment for each property as well as a prescription to be 
agreed upon by the homeowner.  Navajo County staff will mark the property and 
communicate with homeowners to ensure that they are understanding and in support of an 
80 basal area treatment plan. Some properties that are located on steep incline may not 
reach that goal in order to maintain soil retention and avoid other hazards such as flooding 
at the base of some steep terrain where additional homes are potentially impacted.  
 
Once the work is completed the costs will be reimbursed to the property owner by Navajo 
County minus the amount of the match, and any costs over the capped amount 
($2,275/acre) that Navajo County has instituted.   
 
Project Timeline  
Navajo County will look to initiate projects as soon as approvals are received in January but 
no later than February 29th. 
Jan – March 2024 - Quarter 2 – NCEM estimates 5-20 acres will be marked for contractual 
work to be completed. NCEM estimates 5-10 acres will be treated.  
Apr – June 2024 - Quarter 3 – NCEM estimates 5-20 acres will be marked for contractual 
work to be completed. NCEM estimates 10-20 acres will be treated. 
Jul – Sept 2024 - Quarter 4 – NCEM estimates 10-20 acres will be marked for contractual 
work to be completed. NCEM estimates 15-25 acres will be treated. 
Oct – Dec 2024 - Quarter 5 – NCEM estimates 10-25 acres will be marked for contractual 
work to be completed. NCEM estimates 10-20 acres will be treated. 
Jan – Mar 2025 - Quarter 6 – NCEM estimates 10-25 acres will be marked for contractual 
work to be completed. NCEM estimates 5-10 acres will be treated.

<!-- page 815 -->
Navajo County 2023 HFI Narrative  
 
Navajo County - For Official Use Only 
Apr – Jun 2025 - Quarter 7 – NCEM estimates 5-20 acres will be marked for contractual 
work to be completed. NCEM estimates 10-20 acres will be treated. 
Jul – Sep 2025 - Quarter 8 – NCEM estimates 15-25 acres will be marked for contractual 
work to be completed. NCEM estimates 5-10 acres will be treated. 
Oct – Dec 2025 - Quarter 9 – NCEM estimates 5-15 acres will be marked for contractual 
work to be completed. NCEM estimates 10-20 acres will be treated. 
Jan – Mar 2026 - Quarter 10 – NCEM estimates 5-10 acres will be marked for contractual 
work to be completed. NCEM estimates 5-10 acres will be treated. 
Apr – Jun 2026 - Quarter 11 - will be used to finalize treatment of projects, review all 
documentation, submit updates, reimbursements and reports. 
 
All final reimbursements will be submitted by the end of July 2026.  
 
Project Goals, Objectives, and Deliverables 
The goal of these projects is to mitigate the threat of wildfire for as many acres as feasible 
throughout the WUI areas identified in the Navajo County Sitgreaves Communities Wildfire 
Protection Plan. All of the identified communities including of Pinedale-Clay Springs, Show 
Low and Pinetop-Lakeside as well as several outlying subdivisions are within the Wildland 
Urban Interface and would benefit from these mitigation measures. It is estimated that the 
project properties have between a 100-120 basal area pre-treatment.  NCEM will look to reduce that 
significantly to a 80 basal area and in some cases that goal may be higher or lower dependent on terrain 
and vegetation types.  These projects will enhance the work that was completed from 
previous years throughout the region.  
 
Sustainability Plan 
Navajo County will educate homeowners to ensure their compliance with long-term 
maintenance of the projects awarded under this program. Property and homeowners are 
required to sign agreements that they understand this commitment and will manage 
the maintenance on the property without utilizing grant funds to ‘re-treat’ the same areas. 
There will be some properties that will need to be managed over several grant projects as 
some homeowners are not able to provide all the costs up front but Navajo County staff will 
maintain the documentation of what is to be treated and what will not be treated again.  
Additionally, Navajo County will work to continue to provide education throughout the 
various communities by attending public meetings, visiting with HOA's and supporting local 
outreach efforts with booths and information including the annual White Mountain 
Firewise Block Party and the annual Navajo County Fair.

General Provisions  
  
COVENANT AGAINST CONTINGENT FEES  
The Sub-grantee warrants that it has not employed or retained any company or person, other than a bona fide 
employee working for the Sub-grantee, to solicit or secure this agreement, and that it has not paid or agreed 
to pay any company or person, other than a bona fide employee, any fee, commission, percentage, brokerage 
fee, gift, or any other consideration, contingent upon or resulting from the award or making of this agreement. 
For breach or violation of this warranty, the State shall have the right to annul this agreement without liability, 
or, in its discretion to deduct from the agreement price or consideration, or otherwise recover, the full amount 
of such fee, commission, percentage, brokerage fee, gift, or contingent fee.  
  
MODIFICATIONS  
Modifications within the scope of this award shall only be made by mutual consent of both parties, by issuance 
of a written amendment signed and dated by all properly authorized signatory officials prior to any changes 
being performed. Requests for modification sh all be made, in writing, at least thirty (30) days prior to the 
implementation of the requested change.  Any change to the original grant application scope of work or 
approved detailed project plan must have prior written State approval.  Incurring costs without prior written 
approval may result in loss of funds reimbursed.  
  
EXTENSIONS  
Timely completion of this project is required. If this agreement is extended by mutual written consent of the 
parties, all terms, conditions and provisions of the original agreement shall remain in full force and effect and 
apply during any extension period. Any extension of time granted shall not constitute or operate as a waiver 
by the State of any of its rights herein. Extensions will only be considered and/or made if the Sub-grantee has 
demonstrated reasonable efforts to complete the grant project as defined in the original detailed project plan 
and has a clear and specific plan for completion of the project within the extended time period.    
  
RESPONSIBILITY FOR CLAIMS AND LIABILITIES  
The Sub-grantee agrees to assume all risk of loss to indemnify and hold the State, its officers, agents and 
employees, harmless from and against any and all liabilities, demands, claims, suites, losses, damages causes 
or action, fines or judgments, including costs, attorney’s and witnesses’ fees and expenses incident ther eto, 
for injuries or death to persons and for loss of, damage to, theft of or destruction of any property including 
loss of use thereof arising out of or in connection with the performance of duties required by agreement, all 
whether or not authorized or agreed to by Sub-grantee.    
  
RETENTION OF RECORDS    
The Sub-grantee and any subcontractor shall maintain and store all documents, papers, accounting records; 
other evidence pertaining to costs incurred for this work, and shall make all such materials ava ilable at any 
reasonable time during the term of work and for five (5) years from the date of final payment to the Sub -
grantee. The Sub-grantee may be required to provide such records as necessary to any auditing agent. Inability 
to provide such records ma y result in unallowable costs to the grant and any funds disbursed to the Sub -
grantee may have to be paid back to the State and/or Federal government.    
  
COMPLIANCE WITH ARIZONA EXECUTIVE ORDERS 75-5 and 2009-09  
The Sub-grantee shall comply with Arizona  Executive Order 75 -5 and as amended by Arizona Executive 
Order 2009-09 relating to non-discrimination in employment by government contractors and subcontractors. 
These regulations are herein incorporated by reference and made a part of this agreement.

ADMINISTRATIVE AND ACCOUNTING REQUIREMENTS   
It is the Sub-grantee’s responsibility to develop, document, administer and manage the grant in accordance 
with all applicable Federal and State laws.  Sub-grantee is subject to the OMB requirements and guidance in 
subparts A through F of 2 CFR 200 as adopted and supplemented by USDA in 2 CFR part 400.    
  
CFR (Code of Federal Regulations) – http://www.ecfr.gov. If grantee needs assistance in obtaining any of 
these documents in electronic or printed form, please contact your Arizona State Forestry representative.  
  
If any program income is generated as a result of this grant/agreement, the income earned during the term of 
this agreement shall be applied using the deductive method as described in 2 CFR 200.307 ; the deductive 
alternative is the preferred method, unless specifically authorized by the Signatory Official. Costs incident to 
the generat ion of program income may be deducted from gross income to determine program income 
provided these costs have not been charged to the award/agreement and they comply with the applicable Cost 
Principles.  
  
FREEDOM OF INFORMATION ACT  
Public access to grant or agreement records shall not be limited, except when such records must be kept 
confidential and would have been exempted from disclosure pursuant to “Freedom of Information” 
regulations (5 U.S.C. 552).  
  
MEMBERS OF U.S. CONGRESS  
Pursuant to 41 U.S.C. 22, no United States member of, or United States delegate to, Congress shall be 
admitted to any share or part of this award, or benefit that may arise there from, either directly or indirectly.  
  
TERMINATION FOR CONVENIENCE  
The Office of the State Forester, by written notice, may terminate this contract, in whole or in part, when it 
is deemed in the best interest of the State. If this agreement is so terminated, Sub-grantee will be compensated 
for work performed up to the time of the  termination notification.  In no event shall payment for such costs 
exceed the current grant amount.  
  
TERMINATION BY MUTUAL AGREEMENT  
This award may be terminated, in whole or part, as follows:  
• When the State and Sub-grantee agree upon the termination conditions, including the effective date and, 
in the case of partial termination, the portion to be terminated.  
• By thirty (30) days written notification by the Sub -grantee to the State setting forth the reasons of 
termination, effective date, and in the case of partial termination, the portion to be terminated.  
• If, in the case of a partial termination, the State determines that the remaining portion of the award will 
not accomplish the purpose for which the award was made, the State may terminate the awa rd in its 
entirety.  
Upon termination of an award, the Sub-grantee shall not incur any new obligations for the terminated portion 
of the award after the effective date, and shall cancel as many outstanding obligations as possible. The State 
shall allow full credit to the Sub-grantee for the United States Federal share of the noncancelable obligations 
properly incurred by the Sub-grantee up to the effective date of termination. Excess funds shall be refunded 
within sixty (60) days after the effective date of termination.

CANCELLATION FOR CONFLICT OF INTEREST  
Pursuant to A.R.S. §38-511, the state, its political subdivisions or any department or agency of either may, 
within three years after its execution, cancel any contract, without penalty or further obligation, made by the 
state, its political subdivisions, or any of the departments or agencies of either if any person significantly 
involved in initiating, negotiating, securing, drafting or creating the contract on behalf of the state, its political 
subdivisions or any of the departments or agencies of either is, at any time while the contract or any extension 
of the contract is in effect, an employee or agent of any other party to the contract in any capacity or a 
consultant to any other party of the contract with respect to the subject matter of the contract.  
  
FEDERAL IMMIGRATION AND NATIONALITY ACT  
By entering into the Agreement, the Sub -grantee warrants compliance with the Federal Immigration and 
Nationality Act (FINA) and all other Federal immigration laws and regulations related to the immigration 
status of its employees. The Sub -grantee shall obtain statements from its contractors certifying compliance 
and shall furnish the statements to the Procurement Officer upon request. These warranties shall remain in 
effect through the term of the Contract. The Contractor and its subcontractors shall also maintain Employment 
Eligibility Verification forms (I-9) as required by the U.S. Department of Labor's Immigration and Control 
Act, for all employees performing work under the Grant. I -9 forms are available for d ownload at 
USCIS.GOV.  
The State may request verification of compliance for any Sub-grantee, contractor or subcontractor performing 
work under the Grant. Should the State suspect or find that the Sub -grantee or any of its contractors are not 
in compliance, the State may pursue any and all remedies allowed by law, including, but not limited to: 
suspension of work, termination of the Agreement for default, and suspension and/or debarment of the Sub-
grantee or Contractor. All costs necessary to verify compliance are the responsibility of the Sub-grantee. The 
parties agree to comply with A.R.S. §41-4401, the provisions of which are hereby incorporated.  
  
ARBITRATION  
To the extent required by A.R.S. §12 -1518, the parties agree to use arbitration, after exhausti ng applicable 
administrative review, to resolve disputes arising out of this agreement.   
  
ANTITRUST VIOLATIONS  
The Sub-grantee and the State recognize that in actual economic practice overcharges resulting from 
antitrust violations are in fact borne by the purchaser or ultimate user. Therefore, Sub-grantee acting as a 
vendor, hereby assigns to State any and all claims for such overcharges.  
  
SUSPENSION OR DEBARMENT  
Submittal of an offer or execution of a contract shall attest that the sub-grantee or contractor is not currently 
suspended or debarred.  If the Sub-grantee or any of its contractors become suspended or debarred, the Sub-
grantee shall immediately notify the State. The State may, by written notice to the Subgrantee, immediately 
terminate this Agreement if the State determines that the Sub-grantee or their contractors have been debarred, 
suspended or otherwise lawfully prohibited from participating in any public procurement activity, including 
but not limited to, being disapproved as a subcontractor of any public procurement unit or other governmental 
body.    
  
CONTRACTS AND SUBAWARDS TO DEBARRED AND SUSPENDED PARTIES  
Pursuant to Code of Federal Regulations 2 CFR part 180, grantees and sub grantees must not make an award 
or permit any award ( subgrant or contract) at any tier to any party which is debarred or suspended or is 
otherwise excluded from or ineligible for participation in Federal assistance programs under Executive Order 
12549, “Debarment and Suspension”. By entering into this agreement sub-grantee agrees to comply with all 
relevant codes including 2 CFR part 180, subpart C, “Responsibilities of Participants Regarding

Arizona State Forestry grants are based on reimbursement for actual costs incurred. Actual costs may vary 
slightly from the project plan budget, but must be used to calculate final reimbursement amounts.  Sub‐
grantees are typically required to provide a portion of the total project cost as MATCH contribution to 
show local investment in the project or program. Ma tch investment cannot be used as a match for any 
other State or federal cost‐share programs. Specific match amount is identified in each grant agreement. 
All costs and match should conform to the approved project plan and budget contained in the grant 
agreement – and all reimbursements are subje
ct to Arizona State Forestry approval. 
 
Only project expenses incurred during the term of the signed grant agreement are eligible. (See Term of 
Agreement) 
 
All documentation submitted for reimbursement must have the correct project name and/or State 
Forestry grant number, date work was completed, and proof of pa
 yment from the Sub‐grantee. 
 
All reimbursements to Sub‐grantees shall be calculated on the “Grant Reimbursement Form” (Attachment 
E2). By signing the form, the Sub‐grantee assumes full and implied responsibility for all grant costs incurred 
and submitted on the form. By signature, the Sub‐grantee accepts full liabili
ty  that the work and costs 
incurred were in accordance with the agreed scope of work and/or approved detailed project plan and in 
accordance with all applicable Federal and State laws. By signing the “Grant Reimbursement Form”, the 
Sub‐grantee is claiming that costs were incurred following the established procurement proce ss for its own 
organization and that their process is documented, administered and managed with the correct accounting 
and administrative procedures and is in accordance with all applicable Federal and State laws. 
_____________________________________________________________________________________________________________ 
 
INELIGIBLE COSTS – Any expenses submitted for reimbursement that are not properly documented shall 
not qualify for reimbursement. It shall be the Sub‐grantee’s sole responsibility to submit the required and 
accurate support documentation for all project costs. In the event an audit determines that ineligible costs 
were charged to the project, the Sub‐grantee accepts full liability for such costs. 
 
● Expenses not included in an approved project plan or that are unnecessary for the completion of the project 
are ineligible for reimbursement or as match. 
 
● NO FOOD or BEVERAGE purchases or donations to others are eligible for reimbursement or as match, unless 
included in the project plan as budgeted travel costs, and pre‐approved by State. 
 
● Capital Equipment costing $5,000 or more per unit cannot be included as reimbursable costs, but may be 
included as match with prior approval. State Forestry recommends renting equipment as needed. 
 
● NO purchase of equipment or supplies for individuals are eligible for reimbursement or as match (though 
purchase of supplies and small equipment by the Sub‐grantee organizations for ongoing community use may 
be eligible). 
 
● Poorly documented match or volunteer hours with insufficient support documentation will not count towards 
the required match. It is the Sub‐grantee’s responsibility to keep all project/grant records pertaining to 
matching requirements. In the event an audit determines that ineligible match was credited to the project, the 
Sub‐grantee accepts full liability for such costs.

REIMBURSABLE PROJECT EXPENSES – are direct, out‐of‐pocket expenditures for eligible project 
activities that are supported by paid invoices, canceled checks, signed receipts, or official payroll records. 
Examples include: 
 
● Labor (Administrative and Personnel)‐ may include paid staff, or documented reimbursement from 
Sub‐grantee to others for services. Related expenses such as employee benefits or required travel 
costs are also eligible if properly documented. 
○ Administrative labor includes general project oversight, while personnel labor includes work done on 
the ground 
○ All staff/labor hours must be accompanied by an employee time sheet detailing the hours worked on 
the grant project. We must be able to determine, for each staff member, the hours contributed, the rate 
of pa
y, the work completed, and the total amount being requested. 
○ The time sheet must clearly have the State grant ID number, an employee signature, and the dates work 
hours were contributed towards the grant. A supervisor’s approval signature should also be included. 
*Note, for auditing purposes, an auditor will most likel y want to see all hours worked in addition to those 
charged to the grant.* 
○ Required documentation should include some combination of: payment receipts, timesheets, payroll 
records (paystubs), job sheets, canceled checks, or signed letters detailing paid staff time, dates, and 
services or work provided. 
● Contracted Services – Contracting for services from outside organizations or businesses is permitted 
if included in the approved project plan and budget. Such services could include contracted fuels 
crews, arborists, trucking, waste disposal, and other costs. 
○ Required documentation will include original invoices with sufficient detail of work performed, dates of 
work performed, and proof of payment, such as canceled checks or credit card receipts. 
● Supplies ‐ may include operating supplies, office supplies, and small equipment purchased by the 
Sub‐grantee and necessary for the completion of the project. 
○ Required documentation should include proof of purchase via payment receipts, canceled checks, or 
official accounting records detailing expenses and goods and service provided. Original quotes or 
incomplete invoices are not sufficient. 
● Travel ‐ may include mileage reimbursement 
○ Documentation should include mileage logs with beginning and ending odometer readings and 
reference the grant project number. 
● Equipment ‐ may include the cost of renting equipment, fuel, operational costs or repairs at an 
accepted rate 
○ Documentation should include invoices and proof of payment, receipts, or equipment logs. 
○ If using FEMA or negotiated CFRA rates, the non‐emergency rate (½ of negotiated rate) must be used. 
○ Take into consideration that if the rate provided is a "Wet Rate,” it already includes fuel and 
maintenance for the equipment. 
● Other 
○ Other costs as necessary must include proper support documentation demonstrating that the Sub‐
grantee has incurred the costs. 
○ Indirect Costs – Agreed upon indirect costs can be included for reimbursement. 
■ Indirect costs may cover general operating expenses such as those negotiated at the time of 
the grant agreement and other overhead costs; therefore supporting documentation is not

to cover other general operating expe nses.
