4. Environmental Assessment 
Tetra Tech, Inc. was contracted by Enfinity Global to conduct the environmental site surveys 
and assessment. The environmental assessment includes the below: 
I. Wetland Delineation 
II. Flood Plains Assessment 
III. Biological Resources Review 
IV. Cultural Resources Review 
V. Environmental Site Assessment (ESA) – Phase I 
A memo provided by Tetra Tech including the summary of all environmental studies 
conducted is attached as Appendix C. 
I. Wetland Delineation 
Tetra Tech conducted a wetland delineation and preliminary WOTUS 
investigation/determination within the project site on November 20 and 21, 2023.   
No features that met the criteria of wetland horology, hydrophytic vegetation, and hydric 
soils, needed to classify an area as a wetland, were identified in the project area. Three non-
wetland pond features totaling 7.7 acres existed in the project, but these features lacked 
wetland vegetation and are not considered to be potentially jurisdictional wetland features. 
They often existed as unvegetated, dry depressions in the landscape with cracking mud 
bases, likely used as either stock dams or cattle wallows. 
The wetland specialists identified and evaluated eight stream features within the project. All 
these features were classified as ephemeral streams. They exhibited ordinary high water 
mark indicators; however, they did not show characteristics of being relatively permanent 
(having flow for at least 3 consecutive months of the year). They lacked indicators, such as 
a change in soil characteristics, shelving or cut banks, sediment deposits, and the presence 
of litter or debris, that are commonly found in intermittent stream features.

<!-- page 993 -->
10 
 
No stream features within the Project Area had surface water present. It is unlikely that these 
stream features would be considered potentially jurisdictional WOTUS as they do not 
express a continuous surface connection to the Little Colorado River to the north, a 
traditionally navigable water; however, a Jurisdictional Determination would be necessary 
to confirm this. 
 
 Figure 3: Wetland Delineation

<!-- page 994 -->
11 
 
II. Floodplains Assessment 
According to the FEMA panel and the floodplain information portal, a total of nine Zone A 
flood hazard areas (100-year floodplains) occur in the project area, covering 281.99 acres. 
The flooding events are due to the uneven nature of land parcels which will be addressed 
during land grading and construction activities.  
 
Figure 4: Floodplains Assessment

<!-- page 995 -->
12 
 
III. Biological Resources Review 
As per the biological resources review done by Tetra Tech, below were the findings:  
The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service lists four federally threatened species: Little Colorado 
spinedace, Chiricahua leopard frog, yellow -billed cuckoo, and Mexican spotted owl; one 
candidate species, the monarch butterfly; and one experimental non -essential population 
of Mexican wolf as having potential to occur on the project Area. The monarch butterfly 
and Mexican wolf have a moderate likelihood of occurrence. The project will have no effect 
on federally listed species. There is no designated critical habitat within the project area. 
Two plant species protected by the Arizona Native Plant law were found within the project 
area during the on-site survey. No Arizona Department of Agriculture noxious weeds were 
reported in the project area. 
The project area overlaps with a Wildlife Movement Area, and Wildlife Linkage Zone 
identified by Arizona Game & Fish Department (AZGFD) and is within the Apache -Navajo 
County Diffuse Wildlife Movement Area.  These zones identify areas of permeability and 
importance to Arizona’s wildlife and natural ecosystems, aiming to mitigate the effects of 
habitat fragmentation. These designations serve as informational resources only. 
There are no significant biological resource concerns that may trigger permitting 
requirements or other constraints on development of the project.

<!-- page 996 -->
13 
 
 
Figure 5: Biological Resources Review

<!-- page 997 -->
14 
 
IV. Cultural Resources Review 
The cultural resources desktop study identified a total of 15 cultural surveys conducted 
within a one-mile radius of the project. Six of those surveys included parts of the project 
and a total of five cultural sites were identified on the project. These five sites consisted of 
lithic and artifact scatter and were determined to be ineligible for listing.  Enfinity Global 
will conduct targeted cultural surveys at the project, primarily near water  features and 
prepare a probability model to predict the likelihood (low, moderate, high) of cultural sites 
across the project. Prior to construction, Enfinity Global  will prepare an unanticipated 
discover plan that will be used during construction to implement actions to avoid impacting 
cultural sites.  Any eligible sites will be avoided. 
 
 
Figure 6: Cultural Resources Review

<!-- page 998 -->
15 
 
V. Environmental Site Assessment (ESA) – Phase I 
Tetra Tech performed this Phase I ESA in general accordance with ASTM E2247 -16. Based on 
the site reconnaissance performed on November 20 and 21, 2023, interviews, environmental 
regulatory database search report and review of historical topographic maps and aerial 
photographs, no Recognized Environmental Conditions, Historical Recognized Environmental 
Conditions, or Controlled Recognized Environmental Conditions were identified for the project 
site.

is outside of any of these fire districts/departments response, they are the closest to assist in the 
event of a fire.

Woodruff Drainage Evaluation
February 15, 2024
SCOPE OF SERVICES
Project Overview
The Woodruff community in Navajo County (County) experiences frequent nuisance flooding, 
mostly along 1st Street and County Road, due to the lack of drainage infrastructure. Currently, 
runoff flows along roadway alignments in undersized roadside ditches or adjacent properties, 
and ponds at intersections. Runoff generally flows south to north through the community. 
These conditions create impacts to resident vehicular ingress/egress and parking. The County 
would like to investigate the feasibility and cost of drainage infrastructure to better convey 
runoff to the Little Colorado River via improved roadside ditches, storm drain, and other 
mechanisms that may include an open channel drain and/or limited curb/gutter.
The project boundaries Appalusa to the south, the Little Colorado River to the west, County 
Road to the east, and Falcon Lane to the north.
It should be noted that there is FEMA designated floodplain impacting the community 
associated with the Little Colorado River to the west. The Zone AE (with floodway) Special 
Flood Hazard Area associated with the Little Colorado River will not be evaluated as part of 
this project and is outside of the scope of work.
Task 1 – Schedule and Meetings
Following notice to proceed (NTP), Kimley-Horn will submit a preliminary project schedule 
identifying a submittal schedule for the draft and final memo. 
The Kick-off meeting will be held in conjunction with the field visit described in Task 3. No 
additional formal meetings are anticipated prior to project completion.
Task 2 – Data Collection
Kimley-Horn will collect and review existing as-built plans, County Assessor data, and USGS 
topographic data.  One (1) field review will be conducted at the beginning of the project. Field 
review #1 will be to inventory project details, confirm design approach, and verify survey 
data.

<!-- page 1028 -->
Page 3
kimley-horn.com 7740 N. 16th Street, Suite 300, Phoenix, AZ 85020 602 944 5500
Task 3 – Hydrologic and Hydraulic Analyses
Kimley-Horn will conduct hydrologic and hydraulic analyses to assess flow conditions at 
critical points in the project area. Hydrologic analyses will be limited to Rational Method 
calculations for the local contributing watershed not to include the Little Colorado River. 
Kimley-Horn will evaluate 2-, 10-, and 100-year peak flow amounts.
Hydraulic analyses will be limited to normal depth calculations for and proposed roadside 
ditches, open channels, storm drain, and road improvements. Kimley-Horn will coordinate 
with the County on level of service appropriate for proposed improvements based on 
preliminary sizes and construction costs.
It should be noted that these analyses will use the survey provided by the County and 
available USGS topography (10m DEM) only. No new survey will be compiled for this project. 
This may limit the level of detail and accuracy of these analyses and subsequent potential 
infrastructure evaluations.
Task 4 – Alternatives Evaluation
Kimley-Horn will use the results of Task 3 to size conceptual drainage infrastructure to 
potentially include roadside swales, storm drain, open channel(s) for outfalls, and limited 
curb/gutter. In coordination with the County, Kimley-Horn will determine the most cost-
effective conceptual drainage plan as part of this evaluation for construction costing as part 
of Task 5. This task does not include conceptual design.
Task 5 – Cost Estimates
Kimley-Horn will prepare conceptual level engineer’s opinion of probable cost estimates for 
each potential conveyance alternative component, and then an overall cost estimate for the 
preferred drainage plan as identified by the project team.  Kimley-Horn will prepare 
quantities for the preferred drainage plan.  Kimley-Horn will provide estimated unit costs 
based on recent bid tabulations and historic bid database information available from the 
ADOT website. 
Task 6 – Memo
Kimley-Horn will a draft and final drainage memo to summarize the project findings. The 
memo will include a project narrative, hydrology and hydraulic calculations, a list of evaluated 
drainage components, a schematic of the preferred plan, cost evaluations, and quantities for 
selected drainage features. Kimley-Horn will submit a draft memo to the County for review.

Kimley-Horn will respond to one round of comments and submit a final drainage memo at 
project completion.
Additional Services
Items not covered by the preceding scope shall be considered additional services. Kimley-
Horn will provide additional services upon receipt of written authorization from you pending 
agreement between Navajo County and Kimley-Horn regarding scope, cost, and schedule.

2. Environmental Studies
3. Geotechnical testing
4. Public meeting
5. Additional Meetings and Coordination
6. Additional comment resolution
7. Preliminary Design for preferred drainage components
8. Final Design for preferred drainage components
